passages.heading: Meet Josh
passages.text: Commissioner Joshua Wostal is a successful entrepreneur, decorated veteran, and passionate advocate for working families and disadvantaged children. Elected as Commissioner in 2022, Wostal has brought accountability and transparency to the board to stop wasteful spending.

passages.heading: Meet Josh
passages.text: As a job creator himself, he owns and operates a general contracting business. Wostal served our country in the Navy for 10 years and received the Navy Commendation for acts of courage during Taliban attacks on his forward operating base. He has a heart for disadvantaged children and gives back to local children advocacy groups and causes. He and his wife live in the Westchase area of Hillsborough County with their son, daughter, and 3 rescue pets.

passages.heading: The 'Boring' Budget Guy
passages.text: I'm not a politician — I'm just a regular guy who focuses on getting the job done. Here is where I'm fighting for Hillsborough County taxpayers.

passages.heading: End Wasteful Spending
passages.text: Before I took office, I knew our Hillsborough County government was wasting our tax dollars, but I didn't realize to what extent. Most residents don't, because who has the time to comb through an 850-page, nearly $10 billion budget?

passages.heading: Stop the Tax Hikes
passages.text: Here in Hillsborough County, we pay the 3rd highest sales taxes in the state. The county maxes their property tax levy every single year. They impose 3 separate gas taxes. They increased our water bills by 4%.

passages.heading: Fix Our Crumbling Infrastructure
passages.text: Our infrastructure in Hillsborough County is crumbling despite county government collecting billions in tax dollars earmarked for infrastructure. Year over year, our government approved record funding into road maintenance and repaving.

passages.heading: Join the Fight for Working Families
passages.text: Whether you can volunteer an hour, put up a yard sign, or chip in to help us reach voters, every bit of support keeps a taxpayer advocate on the Hillsborough County Board.

passages.heading: Fix Our Crumbling Infrastructure
passages.text: Billions collected for infrastructure. So why isn't our infrastructure fixed?

passages.heading: Fix Our Crumbling Infrastructure
passages.text: Our infrastructure in Hillsborough County is crumbling despite county government collecting billions in tax dollars earmarked for infrastructure.

passages.heading: Fix Our Crumbling Infrastructure
passages.text: Year over year, our government approved record funding into road maintenance and repaving. So why isn't our infrastructure fixed? Well, over the last 18 years, very little of the yearly maintenance fund actually went to funding road and infrastructure repairs—most years as little as 5-10% . The county refuses to maintain our roads and fix potholes, finish connectors, or widen roads to alleviate traffic.

passages.heading: Fix Our Crumbling Infrastructure
passages.text: I'm changing that. I've required all sales tax funds that are meant for infrastructure actually be spent on our roads, not pet projects. I pushed for the removal of the phrase "Community Stadium" from the CIT to ensure the super majority of those funds go to the Van Dyke Road expansion, Lithia Pine Crest widening, and other large scale projects. And I've successfully prevented additional wasteful spending on the Hillsborough Transportation Planning Organization and re-prioritized the I-275 Northbound expansion project.

passages.heading: Fix Our Crumbling Infrastructure
passages.text: Our sidewalk complaints from residents were 16 years behind. We've shaved 6 years off that backlog.

passages.heading: Fix Our Crumbling Infrastructure
passages.text: Another thing that has really concerned me is finding out that our sidewalk complaints from residents were 16 years behind. Residents would trip and fall because of a broken sidewalk, or file a claim to repair uneven walking surfaces that went unnoticed for nearly 2 decades. I made reconciling these complaints a top priority because part of our role as county commissioners is constituent services. My staff and I followed up on these claims, even making house visits, because our residents deserve to know we care. We've shaved 6 years off our backlogged infrastructure complaints, and if elected to another term I will ensure we continue making progress.

passages.heading: Fix Our Crumbling Infrastructure
passages.text: When we spend our allocated funds for infrastructure actually on improving infrastructure, we don't have to raise taxes on our residents. When we have better maintained infrastructure, residents have shorter and safer commutes to and from work, less wear and tear on their cars, and can spend more time with their families.

passages.heading: End Wasteful Spending
passages.text: Who has the time to comb through an 850-page, nearly $10 billion budget? I do.

passages.heading: End Wasteful Spending
passages.text: Before I took office, I knew our Hillsborough County government was wasting our tax dollars, but I didn't realize to what extent. Most residents don't, because who has the time to comb through an 850-page, nearly $10 billion budget? Seeing firsthand the lack of transparency and the fat included in our budget was outrageous. It proved why taxpayers need a budget hawk like me on the county board.

passages.heading: End Wasteful Spending
passages.text: One of the biggest misconceptions is that our county government is broke. It's not. We've been told that year after year, but the reality is our government has been spending millions of our tax dollars on pet projects and giveaways to the commissioners' wealthy friends and campaign supporters.

passages.heading: End Wasteful Spending
passages.text: I'm fighting to put a stop to it. It doesn't always make me popular on the county board, but I wasn't elected to make them happy. I'm fighting to lower our spending to take the burden off our working families already struggling with the rising cost of living.

passages.heading: End Wasteful Spending
passages.text: $235 million of our property tax dollars was funding non-government entities that had zero oversight.

passages.heading: End Wasteful Spending
passages.text: One of the most mind-blowing streams of waste that I recently uncovered was about $235 million of our property tax dollars funding non-government entities that had zero oversight. We found records that show 100 non-government entities making almost $50 million a year, funded by taxpayers. Insiders who made backroom deals were getting rich off us year after year. That's fraud and we're not doing that anymore. We've put new policies in place that ensure these organizations have to apply every year for funding and prove they are delivering results for taxpayers.

passages.heading: End Wasteful Spending
passages.text: In another instance, I noticed the supervisor of elections budget remained the same even after a decrease in registered voters. For the first time in our county's history, I exercised the County Commissioner's Constitutional authority to review the real numbers behind the Hillsborough County Supervisor of Election's budget. We amended about $200,000 and put that money into completing a significant road repair in East Tampa.

passages.heading: End Wasteful Spending
passages.text: I'm running again for Hillsborough County Commissioner to continue bringing accountability and transparency to our county government. I will stop this unsustainable wasteful spending.

passages.heading: End Wasteful Spending
passages.text: I'm the "boring budget guy," and I'm proud of that title. I'm not a politician—I'm just a regular guy who focuses on getting the job done, like I did in the Navy during Operation Enduring Freedom, when I came home and rehabilitated the finances of a struggling family-owned manufacturing company, and in my successful small business.

passages.heading: End Wasteful Spending
passages.text: With your support, I will continue to use my business experience and lean operations background to give taxpayers a voice on the county board. I will continue creating financial transparency so the public sees exactly where their tax dollars are being spent and can hold their government accountable. I will further audit the county's spending, put a stop to backroom deals, and cut fat from the budget. And I will streamline operations and make our county operate fiscally responsible.

passages.heading: Stop the Tax Hikes
passages.text: Tax hikes hurt working families and seniors throughout the county.

passages.heading: Stop the Tax Hikes
passages.text: Here in Hillsborough County, we pay the 3rd highest sales taxes in the state. The county maxes their property tax levy every single year. They impose 3 separate gas taxes. They increased our water bills by 4%. And those are just the ones you can see—there are a lot more buried each year in the budget.

passages.heading: Stop the Tax Hikes
passages.text: I have voted against 4 different property tax increase attempts , and I'll continue to vote no. Our county government has gotten into the habit of increasing taxes to fund their wasteful spending. I guess that's what we have come to expect from politicians, but as a small businessman, I've advocated for identifying more creative solutions.

passages.heading: Stop the Tax Hikes
passages.text: A prime example is our two millage tax approach. 1.1 million residents live outside of the city yet pay into the countywide tax which can't be used on things like roads or safety. I developed a fairer plan that shifts a portion of this tax to the unincorporated millage rate, resulting in an additional $50 to $60 million that can be used for roads, sidewalks, and fire safety. This actually lowered property taxes for residents in the City of Tampa, Temple Terrace, and Plant City and did not increase taxes for unincorporated residents.

passages.heading: Stop the Tax Hikes
passages.text: Seniors on fixed incomes are being taxed out of their homes.

passages.heading: Stop the Tax Hikes
passages.text: We can't continue the same approach that's been done in the past because tax hikes hurt working families and seniors throughout the county. Seniors on fixed incomes are being taxed out of their homes. Families already living paycheck-to-paycheck are struggling to get by. Young couples aren't able to afford to begin their families. Entrepreneurs can't start their own businesses. Poverty is increasing in the county. Residents are going across county lines to buy homes and make purchases.

passages.heading: Stop the Tax Hikes
passages.text: But being creative and thinking outside of the box is what will let our residents keep more of their hard-earned money to spend as they see fit. It will help families thrive. It will help people create generational wealth through buying a home rather than having to rent. And it will help lift the working poor out of poverty and give them opportunities to lead their family to the middle class and beyond.

passages.text: I'm the 'boring budget guy' and I'm proud of that title.

passages.heading: The 'Boring' Budget Guy
passages.text: Before taking office, I knew our Hillsborough County government was wasting taxpayer money, but the actual extent of the problem blew me away.

passages.heading: The 'Boring' Budget Guy
passages.text: We pay the 3rd highest taxes in the state, yet politicians want more of our hard-earned money. I was put on the board by taxpayers who want a leader to roll up their sleeves and get to the bottom of what's really going on with our budget. That's what I've done.

passages.heading: The 'Boring' Budget Guy
passages.text: Our infrastructure in Hillsborough County is crumbling despite county government collecting billions in tax dollars earmarked for infrastructure. Over the last 18 years, very little of the yearly maintenance fund actually went to funding road and infrastructure repairs—most years as little as 5-10%. So where has our money gone? Pet projects and insiders. I uncovered that over $235 million in property taxes were going to fund non-government organizations with no oversight.

passages.heading: The 'Boring' Budget Guy
passages.text: Our county government has a spending problem. To fund their wasteful spending, they keep asking us for more of our hard-earned money. Residents are already struggling—seniors on fixed incomes are being taxed out of their homes, families are living paycheck-to-paycheck, young couples can't start their families, and small businesses are fighting to keep their doors open.

passages.heading: The 'Boring' Budget Guy
passages.text: I'm fighting for you on the Hillsborough County Board. I am bringing accountability and transparency in an effort to stop the unsustainable wasteful spending and ensure our tax dollars are finally being used to fix our county's crumbling infrastructure. I've voted against 4 different property tax increase attempts. I developed a creative plan to change how we tax our residents for mileage, which has increased revenue while lowering property taxes. And I'm finding millions of dollars that should be going towards fixing our roads.

passages.text: Please vote for me so I can continue to fight for the working families in Hillsborough County.

passages.heading: Meet Josh
passages.text: Entrepreneur. Decorated veteran. Advocate for working families and disadvantaged children.

passages.heading: Meet Josh
passages.text: Commissioner Joshua Wostal is a successful entrepreneur, decorated veteran, and passionate advocate for working families and disadvantaged children.

passages.heading: Meet Josh
passages.text: Elected as Commissioner in 2022, Wostal has brought accountability and transparency to the board in an effort to stop unsustainable wasteful spending and ensure our tax dollars are finally being used to fix our county's crumbling infrastructure.

passages.heading: Meet Josh
passages.text: In 2019, he left a successful role as a Chief Operating Officer to set off and become an entrepreneur and job creator himself. For 6 years, he owned and operated a shipping and printing business located next to Raymond James Stadium. From hiring to managing payroll to running daily operations, Wostal handled all aspects of his small business. Continuing his drive as a job creator, Wostal recently began a general contracting business.

passages.heading: Meet Josh
passages.text: Before starting his own companies, Wostal was recruited by a family-owned manufacturing company that had never recovered from the Great Recession. After successfully rehabilitating the company financially, he was named the Chief Operating Officer and doubled the company's revenue. He led the day-to-day operation of the company, driving business goals and creating solutions to better communicate with their customers. In the same role, he was also responsible for quality assurance in areas of technology and finances, giving in-depth financial projections to the Board of Directors and advising on the growth of the company.

passages.heading: Meet Josh
passages.text: He led a 1,000+ person team, managed a multi-million-dollar budget, and served multiple deployments to the Middle East.

passages.heading: Meet Josh
passages.text: For 10 years before Wostal started his career in business and entrepreneurship, he served our country in the Navy as an operations manager. As an operations expert, he led a 1,000+ person team, managed a multi-million-dollar budget, and provided strategic planning and management in the United States and abroad. He completed multiple deployments to the Middle East, including during Operation Enduring Freedom, and received Commendation awards for acts of courage during Taliban attacks on his forward operating base.

passages.heading: Meet Josh
passages.text: Wostal has a heart for disadvantaged children, and his passion is felt in the Hillsborough County community. He partners his business with ChildHelp.org, helping over 1,000 foster children. As a children's advocate, he has volunteered with the Caps for Kids organization and as a Child Life Specialist with All Children's Hospital in St. Petersburg.

passages.heading: Meet Josh
passages.text: He currently serves as Vice Chair of the Hillsborough Transit Authority (HART) and Transportation Planning Organization (TPO), and also serves as a member of Career Source Tampa Bay, Hillsborough/Pinellas Workforce Development Consortium, and the Tampa Bay Water Board of Directors.

passages.heading: Meet Josh
passages.text: He and his wife, Noelle, live in the Westchase area of Hillsborough County. They have a son, Matthew, a daughter, Athena, and 3 rescue pets, dogs named Walt Disney and Piper, and a cat named Lexington. Wostal received his M.B.A. from the University of Florida.
